title: Remote viewing at the Round Table before SRI

tellings.quote: He's basically doing what would be considered remote viewing.

plain: In the early 1950s, years before the government's psychic research at the Stanford Research Institute, a private group called the Round Table Foundation in Rockland, Maine, was already testing what would now be called remote viewing: trying to describe faraway places or objects with the mind alone. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says so, summing up the foundation's records and tape recordings made by its leader, Andrija Puharich. He says that what was going on there was 'basically doing what would be considered remote viewing', which would make the place an early forerunner of the later spy programmes.
